buckets.title: Label the landing page
buckets.description: Seven Oli Gardner-style section labels to keep a one-page, one-goal teardown honest.

terms.title: One page, one goal
terms.shortDescription: Force every element to ladder up to the one conversion that matters.
terms.definition: Give the page a single job—book the call, start the trial, download the deck—and delete or relabel anything that does not point there.
terms.whenToUse: When the hero carries two CTAs, stakeholders debate metrics mid-page, or nobody can answer "what's the one action" in a single verb.
aiPhrases: Act as Oli Gardner and strip this page to a single CTA, labeling each remaining block as either Goal or Noise before rewriting.
examples: Tag hero, proof bar, and footer CTA as Goal-supporting; move blog links into a parking lot doc.

terms.title: Clarity beats clever
terms.shortDescription: Headline answers what it is and why it should matter in one breath.
terms.definition: Name the outcome plainly, then earn the right to be interesting. Cleverness can sit in the subhead once the promise is unmistakable.
terms.whenToUse: When the hero line is metaphor heavy, includes internal brand-speak, or forces a reread before you know the offer.
aiPhrases: Rewrite the hero headline so the first five words answer what the product is and the next five answer why it matters.
examples: Swap "Give your funnels wings" for "Ship CRO-ready landing pages in hours."

terms.title: Visual hierarchy is king
terms.shortDescription: Eyes flow headline → subhead → CTA with zero sideways detours.
terms.definition: Scale, contrast, and spacing guide the scan. Anything competing with the CTA gets demoted, muted, or moved down the page.
terms.whenToUse: When secondary cards, badges, or nav links shout louder than the hero CTA or proof statement.
aiPhrases: Reorder typography and spacing so the eye hits headline, support copy, then CTA in under two seconds.
examples: Reduce partner logo strip to monochrome and drop it below the fold.

terms.title: Attention ratio
terms.shortDescription: One primary CTA, everything else is supportive microcopy.
terms.definition: The attention ratio is 1:1 when there is exactly one action to take per campaign. Links that do not advance the goal either move to the footer or vanish.
terms.whenToUse: When pricing, docs, careers, or social links leak traffic before the main conversion.
aiPhrases: List every link on the page, keep the primary CTA, and recommend where each extra link should move or how to restyle it as supportive text.
examples: Collapse nav to a logo plus CTA for paid campaigns.

terms.title: Conversion momentum
terms.shortDescription: Problem → Value → Proof → Action, zero filler in between.
terms.definition: Each scroll depth builds belief: define the pain, show the promise, prove it, then ask for action. Anything off-sequence becomes a sidebar note.
terms.whenToUse: When case studies appear before the problem statement or CTAs hit before context exists.
aiPhrases: Relabel sections as Problem, Value, Proof, or Action and rewrite until the order builds unstoppable momentum.
examples: Move testimonial carousel beneath the value stack with outcome metrics in bold.

terms.title: Contextual design
terms.shortDescription: Every element nudges the visitor from mindset A to B.
terms.definition: If a module does not advance the mental state—confused → curious, curious → convinced—it does not earn real estate.
terms.whenToUse: When decorative illustrations, generic stats, or culture photos interrupt the story.
aiPhrases: For each section, state the visitor's mindset before and after consuming it; delete or rewrite anything without a shift.
examples: Replace culture photo grid with a comparison table that actually answers objections.

terms.title: Friction removal
terms.shortDescription: Forms, microcopy, and reassurance cues calm every hesitation.
terms.definition: Cut fields, explain why data is needed, and sprinkle microcopy that removes fear right where it appears.
terms.whenToUse: When forms ask for phone numbers too early, privacy reassurance is buried, or button copy feels high-commitment.
aiPhrases: Rewrite the form area so every field has a plain-English label, optional helper text, and a commitment-calming CTA.
examples: Change "Request a demo" to "See the playbook" with a note about 15-minute walkthroughs.
